youtube.title: Why Are American Cars Getting So Huge? (The Rest of the World Isn't)
youtube.description:
Four in five new vehicles sold in America now count as trucks. Why? It isn't just taste. A 1975 fuel law gave 'light trucks' an easier target than cars, a 1963 tariff born in a fight over chicken shielded pickups from foreign rivals, and carmakers built minivans and SUVs to qualify as trucks. Later rules tied fuel targets to a vehicle's footprint, rewarding size itself. The Hidden Why: the true story behind the things you use every day.
#TheHiddenWhy #facts #explained
